supporting_research_snippets.finding: AMEC calls for outcome and impact measurement and rejects advertising value equivalency as a measure of communication value.
supporting_research_snippets.limitation: An unattributed media cost estimate is not realized ROI.

supporting_research_snippets.finding: Observed apply completion varied with application length.
supporting_research_snippets.limitation: Vendor observations can help design a test. They do not identify a causal effect for a new applicant funnel.

supporting_research_snippets.finding: Realistic job previews were linked to voluntary turnover through perceived organizational honesty in a meta-analytic path analysis.
supporting_research_snippets.limitation: Supports an expectations mechanism. It does not identify a client-specific effect or a star-gap threshold.

supporting_research_snippets.finding: A field experiment gave retail managers explicit retention goals and measured quits.
supporting_research_snippets.limitation: A retail management intervention provides a directional precedent, with different context and intervention from coaching elsewhere.

supporting_research_snippets.finding: Favorable applicant reactions related to employer perceptions and reported acceptance and recommendation intentions.
supporting_research_snippets.limitation: Does not establish a universal callback SLA or a conversion uplift.

supporting_research_snippets.finding: A meta-analysis examined effectiveness and design moderators of leadership training.
supporting_research_snippets.limitation: Training outcomes do not establish a client's turnover effect. Evaluate management behavior and local retention separately.

supporting_research_snippets.finding: Accessible forms use necessary inputs, clear labels and recoverable errors.
supporting_research_snippets.limitation: Design guidance, with no universal completion-time target or effect size.

supporting_research_snippets.finding: Reputation, job and company information, and site vividness interacted in business students’ perceptions of recruiting firms.
supporting_research_snippets.limitation: Perceptions from this sample do not establish a site-specific applicant conversion effect.

supporting_research_snippets.finding: Psychological contract breach was related to work attitudes and turnover intentions; the meta-analysis did not find a reliable association with actual turnover.
supporting_research_snippets.limitation: Verify why employees left and test alternative contributors.

supporting_research_snippets.finding: Organizations with a severe 'Say-Do Gap' (where external recruiting claims diverge from Glassdoor/Indeed employee reviews by >1.1 stars) experience 2.4x higher first-year voluntary turnover and a 34% drop in senior offer acceptance rates.
supporting_research_snippets.limitation: Supplied sandbox reference. Verify the magnitude and applicability independently.

supporting_research_snippets.source: Corporate Career Portal UX & Conversion Study
supporting_research_snippets.finding: When an application flow requires account creation and more than 4 form screens on mobile devices, abandonment rates among frontline logistics, retail, and healthcare candidates exceed 58%. Switching to a 60-second mobile fast-apply reduces bounce rates by 30-35%.
supporting_research_snippets.limitation: Supplied sandbox reference. Verify the magnitude and applicability independently.

supporting_research_snippets.source: B2B Employee Advocacy & Earned Media Study
supporting_research_snippets.finding: Employee ambassador posts generate 5x to 8x higher organic engagement than corporate brand pages, while automated tracking reclaims 8 to 20 hours/month of manual HR spreadsheet work and delivers auditable Earned Media Value (EMV) for CFO budget reviews.
supporting_research_snippets.limitation: Supplied sandbox reference. Verify the magnitude and applicability independently.

supporting_research_snippets.finding: Weak middle management and lack of transparent career progression account for over 55% of quantifiable Financial Turnover Risk (EUR) in knowledge-worker and scale-up organizations. Structured 360 feedback combined with manager coaching reduces team-level attrition risk by 18-28%.
supporting_research_snippets.limitation: Supplied sandbox reference. Verify the magnitude and applicability independently.

supporting_research_snippets.source: Academic & Industry Meta-Analysis on Employee Advocacy Readiness
supporting_research_snippets.finding: Asking employees to act as external brand ambassadors during periods of unaddressed workload burnout or cultural distrust produces 'performative backlash'—increasing cynical public reviews and failing to sustain ambassador participation past 60 days.
supporting_research_snippets.limitation: Supplied sandbox reference. Verify the magnitude and applicability independently.

supporting_research_snippets.source: Executive HR Budget & CFO Governance Survey
supporting_research_snippets.finding: 78% of HR budget requests for Employer Branding are rejected or cut because HR presents vanity metrics (likes/reach) instead of Financial Turnover Risk (EUR), Cost-per-Hire savings, and Earned Media Value (EMV).
supporting_research_snippets.limitation: Supplied sandbox reference. Verify the magnitude and applicability independently.

supporting_research_snippets.title: Middle Managers, Personnel Turnover and Performance
supporting_research_snippets.finding: A randomized trial tested what happened when a retail chain gave store managers an explicit goal of reducing employee quits.
supporting_research_snippets.applicability: Use as a precedent for testing a manager-level retention goal. Retail results do not estimate the effect of engineering-manager coaching.

supporting_research_snippets.title: Effects of Realistic Job Previews on Multiple Organizational Outcomes
supporting_research_snippets.finding: A meta-analysis of 40 studies evaluated realistic job previews in relation to hiring outcomes, expectations, performance and turnover.
supporting_research_snippets.applicability: Use to inform a realistic role preview. Check whether recruits' expectations and early exits actually change in the local pilot.

## Three-Phase Action Roadmap

### Phase 1 — Diagnostics
- Audit duplicate handling, reporting effort, source coverage, and ownership.
- Compare starts and submissions by device and role, then reproduce the failure at the suspected form step. — scope: cohort: retail candidates
- Compare dated promises, observed work practices and reasons for exits over a comparable hire window. — scope: cohort: store, store managers
- Compare exits and reported decision rights or manager practices across comparable teams and tenure. — scope: cohort: store, store managers
- Interview target candidates and review conversion for the same jobs and inbound channels. — scope: cohort: Store, HQ
- Agree auditable outcome definitions with Finance. Separate staff time, hiring outcomes and estimated media cost.

### Phase 2 — Scoped Pilots
- Instrument verified tracking steps with source IDs and document staff time and conversion separately. — decision: conditional; prerequisite: Complete the diagnostic and verify the proposed mechanism in this exact scope. Confirm missing or dependent observations against independent records. Specify the affected group and preserve the documented healthy baseline.; pilot design: Build a source-linked ledger for eligible posts and applicant outcomes. Deduplicate posts and report staff time separately from estimated media costs.; preserve baselines: client_internal_context.healthy_metrics_and_strengths_not_to_break#1

### Phase 3 — Scaling Gates
- Expand after completeness, auditability and staff time improve. — prerequisite: Complete the scoped pilot and verify improvements and guard metrics.

## Evidence & Precedents

### Historical case precedents
- **Gamma Retail (Omnichannel Apparel & Lifestyle Chain)** (match score: 0.625)
  - Historical outcome: -19% frontline store turnover within 6 months, +28% mobile applicant conversion, and measurable reduction in store operating disruption.
  - Transfer note: 5/16 root causes match, partial workforce overlap (1/3), same sector, 14 measured T0->T1 deltas
- **BellaModa Retail (Fashion Footwear & Accessories Chain)** (match score: 0.6233)
  - Historical outcome: +31% mobile applicant conversion and -16% store staff early attrition.
  - Transfer note: 4/16 root causes match, partial workforce overlap (1/3), same sector, 14 measured T0->T1 deltas
- **Global Retail Group (Mass Distribution & Fashion Retail Enterprise)** (match score: 0.5689)
  - Historical outcome: +22% Career Website application conversion rate and -35% mobile application abandonment.
  - Transfer note: 3/16 root causes match, partial workforce overlap (1/3), same sector, 14 measured T0->T1 deltas

### Supporting research
- **amec:** AMEC calls for outcome and impact measurement and rejects advertising value equivalency as a measure of communication value. ([source](https://amecorg.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/Barcelona-Principles-V4.0-Ebook-FINAL-Compressed.pdf))
- **appcast:** Observed apply completion varied with application length. ([source](https://www.appcast.io/high-volume-recruiting-strategy/))
- **earnest_2011:** Realistic job previews were linked to voluntary turnover through perceived organizational honesty in a meta-analytic path analysis. ([source](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1744-6570.2011.01230.x))
- **friebel_2021:** A field experiment gave retail managers explicit retention goals and measured quits. ([source](https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2020.3905))
- **hausknecht_2004:** Favorable applicant reactions related to employer perceptions and reported acceptance and recommendation intentions. ([source](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1744-6570.2004.00003.x))
- **lacerenza_2017:** A meta-analysis examined effectiveness and design moderators of leadership training. ([source](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28749153/))
- **w3c_forms:** Accessible forms use necessary inputs, clear labels and recoverable errors. ([source](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/))
- **williamson_2010:** Reputation, job and company information, and site vividness interacted in business students’ perceptions of recruiting firms. ([source](https://doi.org/10.1002/hrm.20379))
